title: Tenure-Track Assistant Professor, Civil and Environmental Engineering
field: Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering
raw_description: Tenure-Track Assistant Professor, Civil and Environmental Engineering. Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering, College of Engineering, Physics, and Computing, The Catholic University of America, Washington, DC. The Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering at The Catholic University of America invites applications for a tenure-track faculty position at the rank of Assistant Professor, to begin August 25, 2027. The search is broad, with a focus on one or more of the following areas: Smart Transportation, Artificial Intelligence in Civil Infrastructure, Geotechnical Engineering, or Structural Engineering. Research Areas: Areas of particular interest include, but are not limited to: intelligent and connected transportation systems, traffic operations and safety, multimodal and transit systems, and transportation data analytics; machine learning, computer vision, sensing, and digital twins for infrastructure monitoring, management, and resilience; geotechnical and geo-structural engineering; and structural engineering, including resilient and sustainable structures. Candidates whose work connects these areas are especially encouraged to apply. The successful candidate will build an extramurally funded research program, supervise M.S. and Ph.D. students, and collaborate with industry, government, and community partners. Teaching: Teach undergraduate and graduate courses in area of expertise and core civil engineering curriculum, advise and mentor undergraduates, and contribute to curriculum development. Reduced teaching load in the first year. Qualifications: Ph.D. in Civil Engineering or a closely related field completed by start date; record of or clear potential for high-quality research and externally funded scholarship; commitment to excellence in teaching and mentoring; P.E. or E.I.T. certification is a plus. The Department offers ABET-accredited B.S., M.S., and Ph.D. programs at an R1 research university in Washington, D.C., with collaboration opportunities with USDOT, FHWA and Turner-Fairbank Highway Research Center, DDOT, WMATA, and DC Water. Review of applications will begin on January 15, 2027, and will continue until the position is filled. Contact: Arash Massoudieh, Ph.D., Professor and Chair (massoudieh@cua.edu).
